extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism adjudication from XML sections, PDF text, and figure captions. The claims are limited to the γ33-41PvD1++ experiments in C. buinensis and do not infer unsupported molecular targets.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: γ33-41PvD1++ permeabilizes Candida buinensis plasma membrane under the source assay conditions, supported by Sytox green labeling after 25 µM treatment for 24 h.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=20:Effect of γ33-41PνD1++ on plasma membrane permeabilization; xml:fig=5

mechanism_claims.limitations: Microscopy assay supports membrane permeabilization but not a unique molecular receptor or binding target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: γ33-41PvD1++ treatment is associated with endogenous ROS signal increase in Candida buinensis cells after H2DCFDA staining.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=21:Reactive oxygen species assay detection; xml:fig=6

mechanism_claims.limitations: ROS increase is retained as a mechanism-associated phenotype, not as proof of a sole killing pathway.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Rhodamine 123 microscopy supports loss of mitochondrial membrane potential/functionality after γ33-41PvD1++ treatment.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The source evidence is a fluorescence phenotype; it does not identify a direct mitochondrial target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: FITC-VAD-FMK labeling supports metacaspase activation after γ33-41PvD1++ treatment, consistent with an apoptosis-like cell-death pathway in the paper.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=16:Results:Detection of caspase activity induced by γ33-41PνD1++; xml:fig=8

mechanism_claims.limitations: Programmed-cell-death framing is preserved as source-supported interpretation; no unsupported upstream target is asserted.

quality_checks.overclaim_guard: No single receptor, exact pathway hierarchy, or image-only quantitative value is asserted beyond the source evidence.
